_comment: What the release being prepared requires of an operator (ADR 0012, ADR 0013).
Authored by hand, like the CHANGELOG's Unreleased section; version and commit
are NOT here because they are derived at build time from the release identity.
`requires_operator_action` is derived too, from whether `actions` is empty.
See docs/self-hosting/release-manifest.md for the field reference.
_bootstrap: The bootstrap constraint is DISCHARGED: 0.1.0 shipped the guard declaring
nothing, as ADR 0013 requires of the first enforcing release - one that
refused traffic the moment it landed would punish installs already doing
the right thing. Later releases MAY declare actions.
The backups-queue-worker requirement stays in the CHANGELOG as prose and
is DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED HERE. This is settled, not pending - do not
declare it because the check now exists.
The check does exist: `backups-queue-consumer` really evaluates, against
a worker heartbeat. Declaring it is what was rejected, because the only
phase it could take is `after-start`, and an unmet after-start
requirement gates SERVING. An install missing a backups worker would
refuse all traffic - the whole support platform down because a BACKUP
worker is absent. Compose stacks start that worker themselves, so it
would only ever fire on host-managed installs, whose operator then has
to edit .env and restart while their site is down.
ADR 0013 has no lighter setting than refusing: phases say WHEN an action
can be performed, not how hard the response is. Until it grows an
advisory severity, a requirement worth reporting but not worth an outage
does not belong in `actions` at all. This one is reported where the
operator meets it instead - the backups page shows whether a worker has
been seen, and says so plainly when none has.
NOTE: tests/Feature/BootstrapSelfEnforcementTest.php still asserts that
NOTHING here gates serving. That was the bootstrap invariant; now that
0.1.0 has shipped it is a tripwire, not a law. The first legitimate
after-start action will fail it, and that test should be reconsidered at
that point rather than the action being weakened to satisfy it.
